author: xiaobin.wu7
caption: Baby Bath Water Level: Too High Can Cause Discomfort—Here’s the Safer Height A common bath-time mistake is filling the tub too high. When water reaches the upper chest/near the armpits, some babies can look fine at first, but may quickly become uncomfortable and fussy as the chest feels “pressed.” A safer setup is keeping the water below the heart—around the belly button to lower chest—so the upper chest stays free and breathing feels easy. Stay within arm’s reach, keep the face above water, and use a non-slip mat for extra safety. #children #ParentingTips #parenting #HealthTok #ChildHealth

caption: 28 Days of Cammie Challenge  October 16th  Go on a walk outside. Camberleigh had two “trigger” words that if you said, and wasn’t immediately ready to do said thing, it was over. Those words were “outside” and “bath”.  I miss deciphering what you were trying to say, I miss playing with you in the bathtub with your toys and bubbles, I miss being able to tuck you in at night.  October 28th 2022 a driver going 75 mph in a 55 mph construction zone was recklessly driving by swerving in and out of traffic when he hit and killed Cammie. He left the rest of the family with lifelong injuries and a lifetime of pain.  The commonwealth of Kentucky looked at his previous speeding record, and the actions taken that day, as well as witness testimony saying “he didn’t even try to slow down” and decided that his actions did not rise to the level of felony prosecution and charges.  So in Kentucky, you can drive recklessly, speed, kill a toddler and injure and entire family, and get away with it. And walk away. Unscathed.  This is a great misuse of justice, and I will not tolerate or stand for it. I will continue to tell her story, I will continue to fight for safer streets because apparently our commonwealth doesn’t see the importance of it like me.  So until there is I’m forever screaming #JusticeForCamberleigh #ForeverAlmost2 #InattentiveDrivingIsMurder #SpeedingIsAChoice #28DaysOfCammie
